grade_reasons: Meets every criterion: 100% of frames have a usable pose; shoulders and hips seen 100%; elbows and wrists seen 100%; 0% of frames followed someone else.
filming_limitations: Side view: the arm and leg farther from the camera are often hidden behind the body.
Body rotation cannot be measured from a side view.

unavailable.label: Cycle time, start to end
unavailable.reason: The clip is too short to compare its start, middle and end: each third needs at least 3 reliable cycles (2 in the start, 3 in the middle, 2 in the end).

unavailable.label: Left-right balance
unavailable.reason: Needs both arms followed through whole pulls. From the side the far arm is hidden behind the body for part of every pull.

unavailable.label: Arm coordination
unavailable.reason: Needs the start and end of both arms' pulls. The far arm's are hidden from a side view.

unavailable.label: Kick rhythm
unavailable.reason: Kick beats are computed but have not been checked against video yet, and the far leg is often hidden.

unavailable.reason: The head turn is not seen reliably from an underwater side view; the experimental detector has not been checked against video.

unavailable.label: Body rotation
unavailable.reason: Rotation around the body's long axis cannot be measured from one side camera. It needs a front or overhead view.

unavailable.reason: Force and efficiency cannot be measured from video of joint positions alone.

metrics.label: Stroke rate
metrics.description: Full arm cycles per minute. One cycle is one full turn of one arm, so both arms together make two strokes per cycle.
metrics.basis: 7 reliable cycles of the right arm, nearer the camera
limitations: From the cycles that could be followed; a short clip covers only a few.

metrics.label: Time per stroke cycle
metrics.description: Median time from one mid-pull of an arm to its next.
metrics.basis: 7 reliable cycles of the right arm, nearer the camera
limitations: Timed to the nearest video frame.

metrics.label: Stroke cycles counted
metrics.description: Whole cycles of one arm between its first and last mid-pull in the clip. Each cycle is two arm strokes (one per arm).
metrics.basis: 7 reliable cycles of the right arm, nearer the camera
limitations: Not the number of strokes in a length: the clip's first and last part-cycles are left out.

metrics.label: Rhythm variation
metrics.description: How much the cycle time changes from cycle to cycle (standard deviation as a share of the mean). Lower means a steadier rhythm.
metrics.basis: 7 reliable cycles of the right arm, nearer the camera
limitations: With few cycles one odd cycle moves this a lot.
It does not say why the rhythm changed (a breath, a turn, the camera).
One video frame is 3.3% of a cycle here, so differences of that size are below what can be timed.

metrics.label: Body line angle
metrics.description: Angle of the shoulder-hip-ankle line against the direction of travel. 0 is level; positive means the feet are lower than the shoulders.
metrics.basis: 7 reliable cycles of the right arm, nearer the camera; level taken from the hip path
limitations: Measured in the picture, from one side camera: movement toward or away from the camera is not seen.
Depends on knowing which way is level in the picture.
Checked on two real clips of one swimmer; not scientifically validated.

metrics.label: Legs against the trunk line
metrics.description: Angle of the hip-to-ankle line against the trunk line carried on past the hips. 0 is one straight line; positive means the legs sit below it.
metrics.basis: 7 reliable cycles of the right arm, nearer the camera
limitations: Measured in the picture, from one side camera: movement toward or away from the camera is not seen.
The kick moves the ankles; the median over each cycle is used.
Checked on two real clips of one swimmer; not scientifically validated.

metrics.label: Head against the trunk line
metrics.description: How far the middle of the face sits above (positive) or below the trunk line carried forward past the shoulders. 0 is in line with the trunk.
metrics.basis: 7 reliable cycles of the right arm, nearer the camera
limitations: Measured in the picture, from one side camera: movement toward or away from the camera is not seen.
The face points stand in for the head; the trunk line shifts a little as the shoulders roll.
Includes the moments of breathing.
Checked on two real clips of one swimmer; not scientifically validated.

metrics.label: Pull depth
metrics.description: Deepest point of the wrist below the shoulder during the underwater pull, for the arm nearer the camera.
metrics.basis: 7 underwater pulls of the right arm (nearer the camera), from where it leaves the front to the last frame it was followed
limitations: Measured in the picture, from one side camera: movement toward or away from the camera is not seen.
Only the arm nearer the camera; the other arm is not measured.
Checked on two real clips of one swimmer; not scientifically validated.

metrics.label: Elbow bend in the pull (2D)
metrics.description: Smallest elbow angle seen in the picture while the arm passes under the shoulder, for the arm nearer the camera (180 is a straight arm).
metrics.basis: 7 underwater pulls of the right arm (nearer the camera), from where it leaves the front to the last frame it was followed
metrics.reason: A picture angle from one camera, not the true joint angle.
limitations: A picture angle, not the true joint angle: an arm bent toward or away from the camera looks straighter or more bent than it is.
Only the arm nearer the camera, and not the end of the push: near the hip and the surface the wrist is often placed wrongly.
Checked on two real clips of one swimmer; not scientifically validated.

metrics.label: Pull path variation
metrics.description: How far each pull's wrist path (relative to the shoulder) is from the average path of the same arm. Lower means the pulls repeat more closely.
metrics.basis: 7 underwater pulls of the right arm (nearer the camera), from where it leaves the front to the last frame it was followed
limitations: Measured in the picture, from one side camera: movement toward or away from the camera is not seen.
Pose noise adds to it, so it never reaches 0.
Only the arm nearer the camera.
Checked on two real clips of one swimmer; not scientifically validated.

metrics.label: Cycle time, start to end
metrics.description: Median cycle time in the last third of the swim minus the first third.
metrics.reason: The clip is too short to compare its start, middle and end: each third needs at least 3 reliable cycles (2 in the start, 3 in the middle, 2 in the end).
limitations: A change in a short clip is not evidence of fatigue.

evidence: Swimming toward the right of the picture, face down: the right side faces the camera.
The right arm's pulls are followed further back (54 degrees more).

cycles.note: All 7 whole cycles of the right arm in the clip were followed.

coverage.summary: 10 of 11 measurements could be made from this clip: 9 met their reliability criteria, 1 are limited.
